title: Leaving the program via a Don't Ask Don't Tell letter

tellings.quote: admitted I said I wrote a letter to my commander

plain: Sometime between 1990 and 1993, a former Air Force sergeant named Dan Sherman says he got out of a secret program at a place he calls Base 2 by writing a letter to his commander admitting he was gay. Don't Ask Don't Tell was the US military's policy that gay service members could serve as long as they kept quiet. Sherman tells Michels this himself, as part of his account of being hired by the National Security Agency, the US electronic spying agency, to talk to aliens, and it shows how he says he finally got away.
